title: MLCase input v1
description: Domain case payload from which the ML adapter derives an EvaluationContract, and the declared experiment topology the leakage rules judge (ADR-0008 decision 3). gates declares the promotion gates a study must clear. The topology is a DAG of declaration sections: each of dataset/split/preprocessing/sampling/selection pins its own version as {identity, sha256}, and split/preprocessing/sampling/selection carry an upstream pin (input_sha256) — split points at the dataset, preprocessing and sampling point at the dataset or the split output, selection points at its upstream stage output; a reference cycle is illegal topology. The schema deliberately admits UNSAFE scope values (full_data, pre_split, test, future_holdout): the semantic leakage rules reject them, and a schema whitelisting only safe values would kill those positives at the structural layer and make the semantic rules unfalsifiable. Missing declarations fail closed (declared-is-the-floor): every section is required, with explicit empty arrays/objects as the considered 'none' declaration. assessment declares the calibration/subgroup/OOD/drift evaluation design in advance (ADR-0008 decision 4); it is a declaration section, not a DAG node. The declaration-vs-result comparison landed in L2 and is adapter-enforced on the evaluation-contract/v2 surface (ADR-0008 addenda A3/A4): each dimension must appear exactly once, a not_performed dimension contradicted by supplied evidence fails closed, and unfulfilled declarations are named as gaps. The L3 semantic layer judges the declared topology's leakage rules.

gates.description: Promotion gates of the case, at least one. Each gate becomes one contract entry; the adapter deduplicates repeated gates when deriving the contract. generalization is the out-of-sample tier (the empirical_claim path; this adapter never produces predictive_claim — ADR-0008 addendum A2).

identity.description: Stable identity of the declared dataset version; one identity always implies one hash, revisions are new declarations.

sha256.description: Content hash pinning this dataset declaration version; the DAG root every split references.

description.description: What the dataset is (source, scale, label space); free-text audit detail, never interpreted.

dataset.description: Dataset declaration: the DAG root. Self-pinned by {identity, sha256}; carries no upstream pin.

sha256.description: Content hash pinning this split declaration version; downstream nodes reference it as their input pin.

input_sha256.description: Upstream pin: must reference the dataset declaration's sha256.

kind.description: Validation contract family (task 2): iid, group (group key in parameters), time_series (gap/embargo in parameters), or nested (inner/outer configuration in parameters).

parameters.description: Kind-specific split parameters (group key, temporal gap/embargo, nested inner/outer folds). Free-form in v1; kind-appropriate keys are a semantic-layer obligation (declared-is-the-floor), the audit obligation lives in the M0 checkpoint.

split.description: Split strategy declaration; reproducible lineage requires the upstream pin to the dataset.

input_sha256.description: Upstream pin: the dataset or the split output. A train_only/per_fold step pinned at the dataset (pre-split) is the scope/upstream mismatch the semantic rules reject.

operation.description: What the step does (for example standard-scaler, median-imputation).

fit_scope.description: Where the step is fit. full_data before the split is leakage; the unsafe value stays schema-legal so the semantic rule remains falsifiable.

preprocessing.description: Preprocessing steps in declaration order. An explicit empty array declares that no preprocessing is applied.

input_sha256.description: Upstream pin: the dataset or the split output (same consistency rule as preprocessing).

method.description: Resampling method (for example random-oversampling, undersampling, synthetic-minority).

scope.description: Where resampling applies. full_data and pre_split are leakage (task 3 sampling clause) and stay schema-legal so the semantic rule remains falsifiable. Required per declaration: a missing scope fails closed at the schema layer.

sampling.description: Sampling/resampling declarations. An explicit empty array declares that no resampling is applied.

selection_scope.description: Where feature selection is fit: per_fold (inside each training fold), full_data (leakage; schema-legal so the rule stays falsifiable), or none (explicitly not applied).

target_encoding_scope.description: Where target encoding is fit. Anything other than per_fold when applied is leakage (target encoding not declared per-fold is rejected); none declares it is not applied.

feature.description: Feature-selection and target-encoding declarations (task 3); both scopes are mandatory so silence is impossible.

family.description: Model family under study (for example logistic-regression, gradient-boosted-trees).

hyperparameters.description: Fixed hyperparameter values for the candidate model. Free-form in v1; an explicit empty object declares none fixed.

metrics.description: Evaluation metrics declared for the case (task 1 metric record). The selection metric is declared separately in the selection section.

search_space.description: Hyperparameter search space. An explicit empty object declares that no search is performed.

split_used.description: Partition the tuning loop draws its comparisons from. test and future_holdout are violations (gate: test/holdout never participate in tuning) and stay schema-legal so the semantic rule remains falsifiable.

seed_count.description: Number of repeated seeds used inside the tuning loop. The schema engine has no numeric-floor keyword; the >=1 floor is a semantic-layer obligation (declared-is-the-floor).

tuning.description: Tuning declaration (task 3/6): search space, the split it uses, and its repetition count.

input_sha256.description: Upstream pin: the stage output the selection drew its candidates from (for example the split output or a preprocessing step output).

split_used.description: Partition whose metric drove final-model selection. test is a violation (gate: the test set never selects the final model) and stays schema-legal so the semantic rule remains falsifiable; future_holdout is not enumerable here at all.

metric.description: The metric the selection maximized/minimized (for example validation f1).

search_budget.description: Declared search budget for the selection (trials, step caps). Free-form in v1; an explicit empty object declares no budget beyond the single candidate.

seed_set.description: Explicit seed set the selection ran over (task 6); at least one.

selection.description: Selection record (task 8): an independent declaration section, field-separated from the final-report evidence so test/holdout metrics never mix into model selection.

status.description: Whether a calibration evaluation is declared for the study.

method.description: The declared calibration method (for example platt-scaling on an in-fold calibration split). Optional at the schema layer: 'declared implies detail present' is a semantic-layer obligation (L3).

status.description: Whether a subgroup evaluation is declared for the study.

group_key.description: The declared subgroup grouping key (for example season or site). Optional at the schema layer (same L3 obligation as calibration.method).

status.description: Whether an out-of-distribution probe is declared for the study.

probe.description: The declared OOD probe (for example a shifted-distribution synthetic holdout). Optional at the schema layer (same L3 obligation as calibration.method).

status.description: Whether drift detection is declared for the study.

method.description: The declared drift detection method (for example a population-stability index per feature between train and holdout). Optional at the schema layer (same L3 obligation as calibration.method).

assessment.description: Assessment declarations (ADR-0008 decision 4): the study's advance declaration of calibration method, subgroup grouping key, OOD probe, and drift detection. Declared-is-the-floor: all four keys are required so silence is impossible, each with status 'declared' or 'not_performed'. The declaration is the evidence floor; the comparison against the assessment evidence actually supplied landed in L2, adapter-enforced on the evaluation-contract/v2 surface (ADR-0008 addenda A3/A4).
